questions.question:
Given the following domain question.
Which customers have purchased Product X?
Which of the following could you represent as relationships in your data model?

Given the following domain question.
What parts of type X are required to make product Y?
Which of the following elements could you represent as nodes in your data model?
When is it a good idea to refactor a data model?
options: When the data model is not performant or does not fill requirements of the business problem.
When the data model has more than 4 relationships.
Never. Data models should be designed to last.

questions.question:
You have a graph consisting of (:Customer) nodes with :ORDERED relationships to (:Products).
Instead of using a direct relationship between Customer and Product to represent an order, what is the benefit of extracting this relationship into an intermediate node Order? Which of the following optimizations involves enhancing the data model by extracting the 'ordered' relationship into a separate node?
options: It enables linking the order to multiple entities, such as products and shipping companies.
It prevents the need for any relationships between Customer and Product.
It allows us to only link products to customers.
It simplifies the graph by reducing the number of nodes.

questions.question: In modeling, the use of bi-directional relationships is a good practice when:
options: The semantics of the relationship in one direction is different from the other direction.
You want to show the same relationship between two nodes in each direction.
This is never a good idea.
A relationship between two nodes could be represented in either direction.

questions.question: What is the recommended limit for the number of labels for a node in a data model?

Before you start a query tuning exercise, you must make sure that the set of queries you will be measuring represents the correct syntax. You can use EXPLAIN to ensure that unnecessary NodeByLabelScan steps occur.
For each query, you should confirm that:
options: An index will be used as expected.
Use correct names for labels, property keys, and property values.
Use literal strings to test values.

questions.question:
Given the Cypher statement below, what are the labels in the data model?

MATCH (p:Person:Customer)-[:PURCHASED]->(order:Order)
WHERE p.name = 'Priya'
RETURN p, order

You are building a recommendation engine for an online store.
Some of their products are perishable and need to be sold within a certain timeframe. Managers would like to find a list of perishable products for stock control purposes.
Which of the following actions should you take when modeling the data?
options: Add a :Perishable label to perishable products.
Create a boolean property named perishable.
Create a :Status node with the name Perishable and create relationships from each product node.

questions.question: What are some things to look for as red flags to investigate in a Cypher query plan?
options: NodeByLabelScan with a lot of DB hits.
Reading property values early in the query plan.
NodeByLabelScan with a few DB hits.

questions.question:
You have a database consisting of (:Person) nodes connected to (:Movie) nodes through :ACTED_IN and :DIRECTED relationships.
What is the benefit of adding additional (:Actor) labels for any (:Person) node with an :ACTED_IN relationship?
options: It provides a faster way to find a subset of (:Person) nodes.
It reduces the number of nodes in the graph.
You can remove the :ACTED_IN relationships altogether.

questions.question: How are relationships treated in graph databases compared to other database technologies?
options: Relationships are treated with the same importance as the nodes they connect.
Relationships are computed at query time using indexes.
Relationships are optional and rarely used.
Relationships are stored as foreign keys in separate tables.

questions.question: When importing data into Neo4j, how should you organize your data model?
options: Represent entities as labeled nodes and connections as relationships.
Store all information as properties on a single node type.
Use only relationships without labels to keep the model flexible.
Store relationships as properties instead of using relationship structures.

questions.question: What type of input does a retriever typically take, and what does it search for?
options: Unstructured input (questions/prompts), searches for structured data.
SQL queries, searches for SQL tables.
Binary input, searches for binary data.
Structured input, searches for unstructured data.

questions.question: In Neo4j, what grammatical form should node labels typically take?
In Neo4j, do all relationships have a direction?
options: Yes, all relationships have a direction that is stored when created.
Direction is optional and depends on the query pattern.
No, relationships can be created without direction.
Only relationships with certain types require direction.

questions.question: According to Neo4j best practices, which of the following would be the MOST effective node labels for a graph database? (Select all that apply)
How are organizing principles stored in a knowledge graph?
options: As nodes in the graph alongside the actual data.

questions.question:
Complete the graph pattern to define a schema in the LLM Graph Builder:

(Technology)-[:HAS]->(Capability)
(Technology)-[:ENABLES]->(Benefit)
In Neo4j, relationship types should represent which of the following?
options: Personal connections like KNOWS or MARRIED_TO.
Node labels like Person or Company.
